asset: 騅 — continuous equine anatomy and articulated limb asset
author: Original project mesh authored by Codex
license: MIT (project license); no third-party mesh or texture imported
sourceKind: Continuous sculpted SDF skin for torso, shoulder, haunch, arched neck, wedge head and ears; closed elliptical anatomical limb lofts around retained joints; tapered swept mane/tail locks
referenceUse: Visual study only. No museum images redistributed and no external assets downloaded.

references.title: Bronze horse, Eastern Han, 25–220 CE
references.use: Period silhouette and elegant pacing horse comparator; later than the story and not proof of exact Qin-Han saddle construction

references.title: Conformation of the horse
references.use: Modern structural reference for shoulder slope, symmetrical muscling, hock/cannon relationship and sloping pastern/hoof transition; no imagery copied

historicalScope: Restrained leather bridle, low padded saddle/cloth and belly girth; no stirrups, high medieval bows or ornate hanging side boards. Interpretive reconstruction, not an archaeological replica.
contacts: Four hoof sole anchors and hip/knee/fetlock joint origins retained. saddleY 1.62 and reinGrips L [0.14,1.86,0.35] / R [-0.14,1.86,0.35] retained. Saddle and rein geometry parented to existing trunk bob; riderBob retained. Explicit setRidden(on) selects retained hand-grip rein geometry while ridden; riderless scenes use reins draped onto the withers/saddle instead of floating in the air.
lod: Distinct cached low/high SDF skins; low elliptical limb ring count 12, high 20; low mane locks 16, high 24. Runtime generated, no binary payload increase.
limitations: Blender Cycles review of actual runtime meshes is independent geometry/material evidence, not game WebGL QA. Existing gait is preserved rather than replaced with a new equine gait solver. Mane and tail are stylized locks, not strand simulation. Original legacy horse fallback is retained for missing FIGKIT.
